extracted.intended_audience: conference organizers, program chairs, and platform engineers running large-scale peer review (NeurIPS/ML community)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and operational criteria for running a large conference peer-review workflow (NeurIPS 2021) on the OpenReview platform, covering recruiting, matching, reviewing, experiments, ethics handling, and post-decision data policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing model (double-blind, closed reviewing, roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS 2021 workflow: double blind, closed reviewing, with area chairs and senior area chairs, and meta-reviews, with the addition in 2021 of rolling reviewer discussion with authors (rather than a single author response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the standard program structure (reviewers, ACs, SACs, meta-reviews). Support rolling discussions between reviewers and authors instead of a single author response period to enable iterative interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruiting and size of reviewer pool
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-scale reviewer recruitment: PCs invited over 13k reviewers, 1k area chairs and 155 senior area chairs; OpenReview leveraged prior conference accepted-author lists (with permission) to aid recruiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare to invite and manage very large reviewer pools and to use external sources (past accepted authors) to seed invitations; plan coordination channels (Google Docs, Slack, video meetings) and 24/7 technical support during high-load periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent user profiles and mandatory registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Require registration of all authors (not just submitting authors) with persistent OpenReview profiles to support conflict-of-interest resolution and multiple contact addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and populate profiles via DBLP imports, author coreference, and staff verification; expect large spikes in new profile creation (e.g., 12,537 new profiles in a month).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts-of-interest gathering and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect extensive conflict information (institution domain names, DBLP URL, Google Scholar URL, institutional history, advisors, collaborators, social connections, and private conflicts) and compute conflicts using institution history, listed relations, and paper co-authorship within the last 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ability to record private conflicts (not shown publicly). Use multiple data sources to compute conflicts automatically to maximize accuracy for matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer expertise modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Build reviewer expertise models using deep learning embedding methods run on titles and abstracts of reviewers' papers; NeurIPS 2021 used OpenReview’s expertise model (instead of TPMS or Semantic Scholar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use automated modern embedding methods to produce affinities for matching; permit program chairs to choose which expertise model to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and draft pre-submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Support draft paper titles and abstracts submitted one week before the full-paper deadline; accept many updates during submission period (e.g., 11,729 submissions with 42k submission updates in final 24 hours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform must handle heavy update traffic, many active simultaneous users, and large volumes of notification emails; monitor CPU and response time to maintain smooth operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding workflow and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs bid on ACs and both ACs and reviewers bid on papers; bidding is tracked as a 'task' not complete until a target number of bids is entered. Bidders can sort by affinity scores or search by metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement task-oriented bidding with progress tracking, sorting by affinity, search, and role-aware bidding (SAC/AC/reviewer differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper–reviewer assignment algorithm and tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Affinity for matching includes expertise model, reviewer bids, and conflicts; matching optimized using Min-Cost-Flow and FairFlow (Kobren et al. 2019). Optimizer meta-parameters are tunable and chairs ran the optimizer many times (∼60 minute turnaround).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide match summary statistics for each output, allow browsing/editing of matches, and support iterative runs with meta-parameter tuning; allow invitation of reviewers outside the initial pool as edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment browsing and manual edits (Edge Browser)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide UI (Edge Browser) to browse match results, explore nested relationships, search, and make suggested edits to assignments while seeing reviewer load and metadata (institution, job title, profile link).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable program chairs and ACs to review and modify assignments with full context (loads, metadata) and invite new reviewers as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized consoles for role-based management
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply specialized custom consoles for reviewers, area chairs, senior area chairs, ethic reviewers, ethic chairs, and program chairs with functionality like task lists, reviewing status, filtering language (e.g., 'papers with missing reviews'), keyword search, reviewer re-assignment, aggregate statistics, bid status, review completion status, email reminders, and CSV dumps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide role-specific dashboards and powerful filtering/searching; support CSV export for offline processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing workflow, visibility timing, and discussion tabs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews are entered directly into the system, visible to ACs immediately, then visible to authors and reviewers of the same paper after the reviewing deadline. Implemented multiple tabs in the discussion forum: author discussion, committee discussion, all reviewing discussion, post-reviewing public discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control precise visibility timing (ACs first, then authors/reviewers), partition discussion into multiple tabs to separate audiences and phases, and record confidential comments separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for confidential comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle confidential comments from reviewers (e.g., recorded 101,112 confidential comments in 2021) separately from public discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide secure storage and clear interfaces for confidential comments targeted to program chairs or ACs only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review quality rating and author feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Area chairs can rate the quality of each review and authors can provide review feedback; these ratings and feedback are visible only to the Program Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect review-quality signals for oversight while limiting visibility to avoid influencing reviewers; use for PC-level monitoring and reviewer management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review configuration and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Add configuration to handle ethics reviews: Ethics Review Chairs assign ethics reviewers to papers flagged with ethical issues; expertise-matching is used to suggest topical ethics reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support a parallel ethics review workflow with dedicated roles, assignment tooling, and integration with expertise matching to identify suitable ethics reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision handling and external editing workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide ability to download CSVs (including AC decisions) for external editing (e.g., Google Sheets), allow PCs to modify decisions, and post/email decisions based on edited sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer data export/import features; consider future direct UI editing or tighter bi-directional integration with collaborative sheets to avoid manual CSV roundtrips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready and post-accept tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Create upload invitations and tasks for accepted paper authors for copyright forms, supplementary materials (including videos), and camera-ready LaTeX zip files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support post-accept workflow with discrete tasks and artifact uploads, including metadata capture and verification steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference track formation via affinity scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide affinity scores between accepted papers to serve as input to paper clustering for conference track assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce inter-paper affinity metrics to help organizers cluster papers into tracks and sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: System scalability and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform must provide smooth service under peak load (example: never surpassed 50% CPU during submission surge; handled thousands of simultaneous users with sub-second response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design for high concurrency, low latency, robust uptime, and large-volume email/notification handling to ensure no degradation during deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review experiments (consistency and resubmission-bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run experiments to measure review consistency (e.g., re-running a variant of the 2014 NeurIPS consistency experiment) and evaluate resubmission bias by asking authors to declare prior rejections and randomly showing resubmission information to 50% of reviewers/ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use randomized visibility of metadata (e.g., resubmission status visible to 50% of reviewers) to measure bias; request authors to describe improvements to discourage resubmissions without substantive change; expect such experiments to guide policy but not to eliminate bias entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author perception survey experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement author surveys to compare authors' perception of their submissions with reviewing outcomes (two-part author survey was implemented; results forthcoming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured surveys post-review to understand perception mismatches and inform process improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision openness and opt-in for rejected papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted papers made public with anonymous reviews, meta-reviews, and author responses. Rejected submissions are not made public by default but authors are given 2 weeks to opt in to de-anonymize and open their papers (and reviews) for public commenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy provides a mechanism for authors to publicly expose potential problems with the review process; expect low opt-in rates (e.g., ~2% in 2021).

rubrics_metrics.name: 24/7 technical and operational support
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview technical staff provided 24/7 support to program chairs, including rapid responses and custom work during submission and reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide continuous operational support during critical workflow windows (submission deadline, notification period) and be prepared for custom feature requests and rapid interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned platform improvements and APIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned features include redesigned paper discussion forum, further improvements to reviewer-paper matching, a new API for per-field visibility control and change-history access, CRON-jobs for automated reminders, synchronous chat-style communications, and live-conference integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design platform extensibility: provide APIs for fine-grained control, support for chat-style synchronous interactions, improved storage/history tracking, and automation hooks to support future workflow experiments.
